context:
Goal: the child repos move to per-lane merge without losing open work or a way back.
Problem (rule): your ruling Q1 a (2026-11-12 09:42 CST, decision all-repos-switch-together) says all repos switch together; no repo switches alone. The shared merge tool now has no batch build on main 59da758a3. Child repos still batch through an older installed copy (f1b8031f1): q_max, ios-adblock, banchi, mailaudit (#323 queued) and degen (#702 held on a queued Mac run). Refreshing a child's install removes --batch-build there. The decision says each child needs the stable branch and the revert route first.
Based on (read): batch runner 11's read, 15:27 CST (home, joyous and the rest unknown), the coordinator's 15:27 note, and the decision text on main. Triage has not read the child repos' PRs.
Departs from: main — children batch today on the old install; both options end that, at different times.
Meanwhile: runner 11 starts no new batch and keeps its install; nothing refreshes.

options.gain: No open batch work is stranded, and it stays within your "switch together" ruling.
options.label: Pin each child's install at f1b8031f1, finish its open batch PRs, then switch every repo at one agreed moment, each with its stable branch and revert route (Recommended)
options.lose: Children batch longer on a tool that is no longer maintained.

options.label: Switch all child repos now
options.lose: Open batch PRs (mailaudit #323, degen #702) lose their path, and children may lack the stable branch or revert route.

No action from you. Only item 767 (drain) is yours.
short: When do the child repos switch to per-lane merge?
title: Switch the child repos to per-lane merge after they finish their open batches, or now?
why: Refreshing a child's merge tool removes batching there, and your ruling says no repo switches alone.
